newsitem.title: USA: Christopher Reeve asks Congress for more funds.
newsitem.headline: Christopher Reeve asks Congress for more funds.

text.p: Actor Christopher Reeve, paralyzed in a horse-riding accident two years ago, made an impassioned plea to Congress on Thursday to devote more money to research brain and spinal cord injuries.

Addressing a Senate appropriations subcommittee on advances in research on brain and spinal cord injuries, the former "Superman" movie star said progress was being made to find a cure for these injuries but more funding was needed.
"We must not stop this progress because we are unwilling to commit enough money to get the job done," he told the panel, which examines funding for medical research.

"It is imperative the public and more importantly our elected representatives understand that research today is not speculative. It is not a waste of money," added Reeve, who has become an advocate for people with disabilities.
Speaking to the panel from his wheelchair, Reeve said the investment of "real dollars" was needed -- money that did not fit within the constraints of budgetary amendments.

Reeve, an accomplished rider who owns several horses, suffered multiple injuries including two shattered neck vertebrae when he was thrown from his horse at an equestrian event in Commonwealth Park in Culpepper, Virginia, on May 27, 1995.
In an interview on CBS News "48 Hours" program last month, Reeve said he had started to regain feeling in his arms, hands and back.
His doctors said Reeve's progress was "phenomenal" but that it was too early to tell whether he would walk again.
During his stage and screen career, Reeve was best known for the "Superman" films based on the comic-book hero in which he played the fumbling Clark Kent who at will turns into the flying superhero.

Since his accident, Reeve has directed a television movie, appeared at the Academy Awards and the Democratic Party's national convention. He travels the country raising money and speaking on behalf of the disabled.
